places.name: The Potentate's Works

why.founding: Versidue-Shaie was the Akaviri Potentate, and the works his people left in this basin while building the Rose are not Cyrodilic in any detail.
why.siteAdvantages: On the quarry road between the Robbed City and the Rose — the logistics of a single-day construction, made permanent.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. Its stone-handling gear was designed for atronachs and makes no sense for people.
why.pressures: It is the best surviving Akaviri civil work in the province and nobody in the basin knows what it is.
why.wouldChangeIf: An identification would bring outside scholars and their money into a district that wants neither.

preferences.neighbourRelation: under or beside later Imperial works

vibe.palette: Grey dressed stone, unusual tooling, green invasion.
vibe.signatureFeature: A stone-handling yard with lifting sockets sized for something inhumanly strong, and Akaviri tool-marks on every dressed face.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance (70 records against a 17-21 budget): tier-2 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.

why.founding: A karst chamber in the lake's limestone shore that holds a bubble of air above the water line, entered from below.
why.siteAdvantages: Three metres under the shore cliff, opening into a dry chamber the size of a room.
why.occupantsMotive: Used as a cache by whoever currently needs a place no search will find.
why.pressures: The air is old and the chamber is silent enough to hear the lake through the rock.
why.wouldChangeIf: A rise in lake level would flood the bell and drown whatever is in it.

preferences.neighbourRelation: hidden; discovered by exploring water

vibe.silhouette: No exterior at all — a cliff-foot shore with nothing to see, and a dry room hidden three metres under it.
vibe.palette: Wet limestone cream, black water, lamp gold.
vibe.materials: Natural limestone dome, one natural stone shelf used as a store, oiled hide wrappings on the goods, a single lamp; nothing built, nothing fixed.
vibe.signatureFeature: A dry limestone room reached only by swimming down and up again, with dry goods stacked on a natural shelf.
vibe.condition: Undisturbed and in constant use — the goods change, the room never does.
vibe.approach: Swim down along the cliff foot and up again; the first thing you know of it is your head breaking into air.
vibe.senses: A ringing dead air like the inside of a bell; drips on a long slow beat; lamp-oil; dry sacking after cold water.

places.name: The Running Post

why.founding: Three rivers and a lake mean letters go by boat and arrive late; the runners exist because the causeway road is faster than the water.
why.siteAdvantages: At the junction of the causeway road and the lake shore, with fresh runners always waiting.
why.occupantsMotive: Runners are paid by the delivery and race each other for the good routes.
why.pressures: Everything to and from the Rose passes through here and some of it is read.
why.wouldChangeIf: A regular ferry timetable would make the runners obsolete on two of their three routes.

preferences.neighbourRelation: chained; a relay that does not reach its neighbour is not a relay

vibe.palette: Chalk white, dust, running-leather brown.
vibe.signatureFeature: A post with a peg board of destinations, a bench of waiting runners, and a chalked record of the day's best times.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance: type 'courier-relay' runs 10 province-wide against a countBand of 7-9, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

places.name: The Counting Stones

why.founding: Nineteen dressed stones standing in the marsh in a line that points at nothing, older than the Lilmothiit city.
why.siteAdvantages: On a firm ridge under the marsh that only becomes apparent when you walk the line.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. Villages count them on passing and disagree about the total, which is a local joke with an edge to it.
why.pressures: Two stones have fallen and been re-erected in the wrong sockets, which nobody living noticed.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing explains them. Every proposed explanation has been wrong.

preferences.neighbourRelation: deliberately unrelated to its surroundings

vibe.palette: Grey stone, reed gold, flat water.
vibe.signatureFeature: Nineteen worked standing stones in a dead-straight line across marsh, with two of them subtly out of true and their empty sockets beside them.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance (70 records against a 17-21 budget): tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.

places.name: The Cordon Hearth

why.founding: A kept fire on the southern approach, built against one of the cordon stones because that was the only marker on the road.
why.siteAdvantages: At the midpoint of an eight-kilometre stretch with no settlement.
why.occupantsMotive: Kept by Rockspring on a rota, badly in winter and well in the trading season.
why.pressures: Travellers who know the district avoid sleeping here because of what the stone next to it means.
why.wouldChangeIf: Moving it two hundred metres would double its use, and nobody will move it.

hardConstraints: on a route, with a landing

preferences.neighbourRelation: chained along routes at a day's travel; the province's D0 floor outside cities

vibe.palette: Fire orange, cordon-stone grey, dark road.
vibe.signatureFeature: A hearth house built physically against a plague cordon marker, using the stone as one wall.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance (70 records against a 17-21 budget): tier-4 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.

places.name: The Fasting Hut

why.founding: An ascetic who took a rock ledge above the sinkhole because the sound of the water going down is, they say, the point.
why.siteAdvantages: A dry ledge above a sinkhole with a spring within reach and no approach that is not deliberate.
why.occupantsMotive: They eat what pilgrims bring and answer questions in exchange for nothing.
why.pressures: They know the basin's water routes better than anyone alive and give the information away, which the drag crew resents deeply.
why.wouldChangeIf: Their death would take the district's best hydrological knowledge with it.

preferences.neighbourRelation: deliberately far from everything; the effort-to-reach IS the design

vibe.palette: Grey limestone, white water, thin smoke.
vibe.signatureFeature: A ledge hut above a roaring sinkhole, with the district's water routes scratched into the rock face beside the door.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance: type 'hermit-hut' runs 9 province-wide against a countBand of 5-6, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

places.name: Basin Swallow

why.founding: A limestone sinkhole in the western hills that takes an entire stream underground and does not give it back anywhere anyone has found.
why.siteAdvantages: A genuine rarity in this province — the scour found eleven sinkholes province-wide, and this is the only one in the basin.
why.occupantsMotive: Nothing lives on the rim. Something lives below the first ledge.
why.pressures: It is almost certainly connected to the Blue Hole, and nobody has proved it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Proving the connection would open a route from the western hills into the lake floor.

preferences.neighbourRelation: rare — eleven found province-wide; every instance should be individually meaningful

vibe.palette: Grey limestone, white falling water, black throat.
vibe.signatureFeature: A vertical shaft in dry limestone with a stream pouring into it and no sound of it landing.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance: type 'sinkhole-mouth' runs 4 province-wide against a countBand of 3-3, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

places.name: The Gatehouse

why.founding: A family living in the gatehouse of the abandoned cordon fort, because it has a roof and a door and nobody has ever asked them to leave.
why.siteAdvantages: The one part of the fort that is dry, defensible and small enough to heat.
why.occupantsMotive: They keep the road, sell water to travellers and consider themselves the fort's caretakers.
why.pressures: They are also the first thing any faction occupying the fort would have to deal with.
why.wouldChangeIf: A garrison would evict them in an afternoon.

preferences.neighbourRelation: inside any ruin type

vibe.palette: Lamp yellow in grey stone, painted board, road dust.
vibe.signatureFeature: One lit window in the gatehouse of an otherwise dark fort, with a water butt and a hand-painted price beside the road.
vibe.mood: Small life in a large shell.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance: type 'squatted-ruin-home' runs 5 province-wide against a countBand of 4-4, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

places.name: The Standing Account

why.founding: A tradehouse on the causeway road where the Rose's people and the city's people can drink in the same room, which is the whole point of it.
why.siteAdvantages: Halfway along the road, on firm ground, with a landing behind it.
why.occupantsMotive: The keeper runs a standing account for both sides and has never once been robbed.
why.pressures: Everything said here reaches both the city and the Rose within a day.
why.wouldChangeIf: A killing here would close the only neutral room in the district.

hardConstraints: on a route, with a landing

preferences.neighbourRelation: on every real route at day-travel spacing; in every M3+ settlement

vibe.palette: Hearth glow, slate grey, worn plank.
vibe.signatureFeature: A long room with two hearths at opposite ends and a slate of standing accounts kept in two columns.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance (70 records against a 17-21 budget): tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.

places.name: Blackrose

why.founding: Built by the Lilmothiit in a lake where three rivers converge; rebuilt by the Empire after 1E 2837 and held since by whoever holds the island core.
why.siteAdvantages: The hinge of the south: Murkwood's water from the north-east, Oliis Bay from the south, eastern Blackwood from the west, and Bramman's concealed river out to Topal Bay.
why.occupantsMotive: Toll and transit revenue, and whatever comes out of the Rose. Many have entered its walls; the city keeps the ones who do not leave.
why.pressures: It remembers raising an army against the Third Empire and remembers a battlemage breaking it with a single spell; it distrusts magic and outsiders in that order.
why.wouldChangeIf: Whoever took the island core would take the whole southern route network with it, which is why the core has changed hands four times.

hardConstraints: island in standing water at a confluence

preferences.neighbourRelation: lake hub; a notorious prison a day's march north
preferences.densityGradient: city core; dense over water, thin on land

occupants: a resident An-Xileel delegation nobody will house

vibe.silhouette: A dark walled island core with a single spire of Lilmothiit footing carried up in Imperial courses, standing clear above a flat spread of boardwalk roofs that reaches to three gates on three rivers.
vibe.palette: Grey lake water, dark wet stone, red-brown Argonian roofs, lamp reflections.
vibe.materials: Three courses of history in one wall: Lilmothiit foundation blocks, Imperial dressed courses on top, and Argonian roof and boardwalk carpentry over both — the stone is inherited, never quarried, and the timber is all new.
vibe.signatureFeature: A walled stone core on a lake island — Lilmothiit foundations, Imperial courses, Argonian roofs — with the rest of the city spread over the water on boardwalks between three river gates.
vibe.condition: Continuously repaired for two thousand years and never once finished: fresh mortar in ancient joints, new decking on old piles, four different centuries of gate ironwork.
vibe.approach: The core reads across open water from every river gate, lit, with its reflection under it — the province's one genuine approach vista.
vibe.senses: Gate bells answering across open water, oars and toll-chains, wet stone and lamp oil, and the flat sound a big lake makes when a city is built on it.

places.complexityJustification: A major city: a walled island core over Lilmothiit foundations plus stilt and boardwalk districts spread across a lake, with three river gates. Compiled from the blueprint schema.

localStateVariants.description: The island core has changed hands; the gates are shut and the boardwalk city is trading around them.
Wet-season high water: the boardwalk city floats a metre higher and the lower gate is unusable.

why.founding: Blackrose's Hist stands in the lake rather than in the city, and the lake rose over it — the register's drowned tree.
why.siteAdvantages: It grew on the island's old shore; three centuries of raised lake level put six metres of water over its crown.
why.occupantsMotive: Tenders dive to it. The city has no other tree and will not plant one, because planting one would be a judgement on this one.
why.pressures: An underwater Hist cannot be communed with in any of the usual ways, and the tenders have improvised a practice nobody else recognises.
why.wouldChangeIf: Lowering the lake would expose it — and it is not agreed whether that would save it or kill it.

preferences.neighbourRelation: tended from a nearby settlement

vibe.silhouette: A green shadow the size of a village six metres down, with weighted offering lines running from a small surface platform straight into it.
vibe.palette: Green underwater light, dark bark, silver surface.
vibe.materials: Living drowned hardwood and its intact canopy; a surface platform of lashed timber; weighted offering lines of cord, shell and tin — nothing built on the tree itself.
vibe.signatureFeature: A great tree standing whole and alive underwater, its canopy a green shadow six metres down, with weighted offering lines running from a boat platform on the surface.
vibe.condition: Alive and wholly submerged; the tree is undamaged, the platform above it is rebuilt every few years.
vibe.approach: Poled out to a small platform in open water with nothing to see, and then you look down.
vibe.senses: Above, only the creak of the platform and the lines running; below, green light through leaves that should be in air, and the root-hum coming up through the water into your chest.

localStateVariants.description: Drawdown has put the crown within a metre of the surface and the whole district has come to see it.

places.name: Blackrose Prison

why.founding: Built by Potentate Versidue-Shaie's battlemage Pelladil Direnni out of the rubble of the ancient Lilmothiit city, by an army of stone atronachs, in a single day, a day's march south of Blackrose.
why.siteAdvantages: Marsh on every side and one causeway: the Imperial siting rule for this province, executed perfectly.
why.occupantsMotive: Prison-born families three generations deep who hold it as their inheritance, plus exiles and outlaws; they resent being called a prison and have a real argument that they are not one.
why.pressures: Umbriel left something in the lower levels that nobody has cleared; the Chainbreakers want the place opened; Blackrose wants the toll it takes on the south road.
why.wouldChangeIf: Clearing the lower levels would make the Rose a genuine settlement, and everybody who benefits from its reputation knows it.

preferences.neighbourRelation: a day's march from a city that pretends it is not there

notableNpcSlots: the one person who remembers what was bricked up
Chainbreaker envoy camped on the causeway

vibe.silhouette: A blunt single-day fortress with no architectural intent at all — flat curtain, flat towers, blocks laid at whatever angle they came out of the rubble — softened by washing lines strung across the yard.
vibe.palette: Grey re-cut stone, ochre carving fragments, black stairwell, domestic colour in the yard.
vibe.materials: Reused Lilmothiit stone throughout, vulpine carving surviving at random angles in the courses; Imperial iron gate furniture; and inside the yard, three generations of purely domestic Argonian carpentry that never touches the walls.
vibe.signatureFeature: A single-day fortress of reused Lilmothiit stone, its blocks still carrying vulpine carving laid in at random angles, with washing lines strung across a parade yard and a sealed stair to the lower levels.
vibe.condition: Fortification unbreached and unrepaired because it needs none; the interior wholly domesticated; one stairwell bricked and mortared two generations ago.
vibe.mood: Domestic on the surface, wrong beneath.
vibe.approach: One causeway across open marsh, watched from the moment you step onto it.
vibe.senses: Children in a parade yard; a wall that swallows sound; cold coming off the sealed stairwell in the corner of a warm yard; cooking, washing, goats.

places.complexityJustification: A canon fortress-prison with three occupancies stacked in it (prison-born families, outlaws, and Umbriel's dead below) and a defended approach — the zone's largest single authored site.

localStateVariants.description: The bricked stair is open; the yard has emptied and the families are camped on the causeway.
Blackrose is holding the causeway; nothing enters and the yard is rationing.

places.name: The Refused Vault

why.founding: A vault for the ashes of those the basin's villages refused to stake — blasphemers, oath-breakers and, latterly, anyone who died in the Rose unclaimed.
why.siteAdvantages: Cut into the limestone above the flood, deliberately far from any burial ground.
why.occupantsMotive: A keeper who accepts urns and refuses to discuss any of them.
why.pressures: The Chainbreakers argue that the prison dead here were refused for the wrong reason and want them out.
why.wouldChangeIf: A ruling that the prison dead may be staked would empty half the vault.

preferences.neighbourRelation: deliberately outside a village's normal ground

vibe.palette: Grey rock, terracotta urn, lamp shadow.
vibe.signatureFeature: A rock-cut vault of stacked urns, each with a single word on it explaining the refusal, and a growing section where the word is the same on every one.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance: type 'urn-vault' runs 4 province-wide against a countBand of 2-2, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

places.name: The Cold Bloom

why.founding: A bloomery working the basin's bog iron, abandoned when the charcoal ran out rather than the ore.
why.siteAdvantages: Beside the ore beds with water for the bellows and, once, woodland for the charcoal.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The furnace stack stands and the slag heap is the highest ground for two kilometres.
why.pressures: The ore is still there and the charcoal still is not; nothing has changed the arithmetic.
why.wouldChangeIf: A charcoal supply from the eastern forest would restart it tomorrow.

preferences.neighbourRelation: near a road or a foreign settlement

vibe.palette: Slag black-purple, rust, reed gold.
vibe.signatureFeature: A furnace stack standing alone on a slag heap that has become the local high point, with the last bloom still in the hearth.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance: type 'bog-iron-bloomery' runs 3 province-wide against a countBand of 2-2, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

places.name: Bramman's Head

why.founding: The inland end of the concealed river a First-Era fleet sailed up from near Soulrest: where Bramman's water finally meets the Blackrose lakes.
why.siteAdvantages: A screened lagoon head with just enough depth for a laden hull, and a bank firm enough to tranship on.
why.occupantsMotive: A small permanent crew who keep the head open, charge for the last mile, and have never let the route be charted.
why.pressures: Blackrose's toll authority knows the head exists and has never been able to find its mouth.
why.wouldChangeIf: Charting the river would make Blackrose a sea port and destroy the pilots at both ends.

preferences.neighbourRelation: the hinge between a boat lane and a land route; a mandatory node

notableNpcSlots: lagoon pilot who decides who is brought in
Night-Reed fence working out of a tent

vibe.silhouette: No silhouette — a blind lagoon head screened by mangrove, with a cut stone bank at the back of it that you cannot see until you are in the lagoon.
vibe.palette: Black water, green screen, old iron.
vibe.materials: Ancient cut mooring bank with thousand-year-old iron rings, fresh rope on every ring, market tents and scaffold shears struck between uses; nothing permanent above the bank.
vibe.signatureFeature: A stone-cut mooring bank in a blind lagoon, with iron rings a thousand years old and a fresh rope on every one of them.
vibe.condition: The stonework is ancient and perfect; everything above it is deliberately temporary.
vibe.approach: Through a screen of mangrove that closes behind you, into a lagoon with a working quay in it that nobody outside knows exists.
vibe.senses: The bay noise cutting off as the screen closes behind you; rope on old iron; whispered tallying; still black water.

localStateVariants.description: The screen route is compromised; the lagoon is empty and the rings have no rope on them.

places.name: The Floating Road

why.founding: The land route to the Rose crosses four kilometres of marsh that will not carry a stone causeway, so it is built to float and rise with the flood.
why.siteAdvantages: Deep soft marsh with a stable water level: the one place where a floating road works better than a built one.
why.occupantsMotive: Maintained by Vaunting, whose whole existence depends on it, section by numbered section.
why.pressures: It moves underfoot, it cannot be defended, and it is the only way the Rose is supplied.
why.wouldChangeIf: Cutting three sections would isolate the Rose completely, which several parties have considered.

preferences.neighbourRelation: links two named places directly

vibe.palette: Wet dark timber, marsh olive, painted section numbers.
vibe.signatureFeature: A road of lashed buoyant timber rafts numbered along its whole length, re-pegged at both ends each season so the deck sits about a metre higher in the wet than in the dry.
vibe.approach: You can see the whole crossing from either end and be seen for all of it.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance (70 records against a 17-21 budget): tier-2 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.

localStateVariants.description: Wet season: the deck rides high, the end ramps are steep and the numbered sections are re-pegged.
Dry season: the deck sits low on the mud, the ramps are flat and two sections are grounded.

places.name: The Lit Pool

why.founding: A spring-fed cave pool in the limestone whose water glows year-round, and which the basin's villages have used as a light source for centuries.
why.siteAdvantages: A cave mouth at the foot of the western hills with a permanently full clear pool.
why.occupantsMotive: Lamp-jelly gatherers take a fixed quantity by an agreement that predates the city.
why.pressures: Two villages' quotas overlap and the argument is annual and ritualised.
why.wouldChangeIf: A drop in the spring would end the glow and a very old argument.

preferences.neighbourRelation: known and visited; a destination, not a secret

vibe.palette: Blue-green glow, wet limestone, black cave.
vibe.signatureFeature: A cave pool that lights the whole chamber blue-green from below, with quota marks cut into the rock at the waterline.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance: type 'bioluminescent-water' runs 6 province-wide against a countBand of 4-5, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

why.founding: The Blackrose Chainbreakers' shelter for people who have come out of the Rose, an Owing, or a toll pit, and have nowhere that will take them.
why.siteAdvantages: Outside the toll line, on water, with two exits and no fixed sign.
why.occupantsMotive: Board, work and legal help; the Chainbreakers' whole practical programme in one building.
why.pressures: Two of the powers they oppose fund half their neighbours, and the shelter is watched constantly.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single violent incident here would let the city close it lawfully.

preferences.neighbourRelation: within a day of a hard owing district, out of its sight

vibe.silhouette: A rambling low water-house that has grown sideways rather than up, with more doors than windows and no sign of any kind.
vibe.palette: Patched timber, lamp gold, tag-bone white.
vibe.materials: Mud-mother plaster and patched shack-kit over a stilt frame, market canvas over the yard, a wall of hung bone-tags; every material second-hand.
vibe.signatureFeature: A rambling water-house with more doors than rooms, a work-board of paid tasks, and a wall of returned bone-tags from the Rose.
vibe.condition: Perpetually extended and never finished — a new room whenever a new group arrives.
vibe.approach: Reached by water from two directions, with no sign and no landing stage — you are told which door, or you do not find it.
vibe.senses: Constant arrivals; the tag wall clicking in the draught; cooking for more people than expected; lamp oil; nobody asking anybody's name.

localStateVariants.description: The Owing brokers have found it; the doors are shut and the tag wall is stripped.

places.name: The Chain Towers

why.founding: A chain of three low towers linking the city to the Rose causeway, built so a signal could cross the marsh in minutes.
why.siteAdvantages: Sited on the only three rises with mutual sightlines across four kilometres of flat marsh.
why.occupantsMotive: Manned by the toll families, who use the chain for commercial news far more than for alarms.
why.pressures: The Rose can see the towers and reads the signals perfectly well.
why.wouldChangeIf: A single lost tower breaks the chain and the city's early warning with it.

hardConstraints: commands a route or a channel

preferences.neighbourRelation: must see a neighbour, or it is not a watch tower

vibe.palette: Grey stone, marsh olive, lamp shutter black.
vibe.signatureFeature: Three squat towers in a line across flat marsh, each visible from the next, with shuttered signal lamps and nothing else in them.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance (70 records against a 17-21 budget): tier-3 density fill on the province's most over-dense ground.

places.name: The Reading Ledge

why.founding: A cliff bench on the western hills from which the entire lake, all three river mouths and the Rose's causeway can be seen at once.
why.siteAdvantages: The only ground above the basin with a clear line over the whole of it.
why.occupantsMotive: Used by the city's signal watch, by the toll families, and by everyone planning anything.
why.pressures: Whoever holds this ledge sees every movement in the basin a full hour before the city does.
why.wouldChangeIf: Nothing changes it, which is why it has been fought over twice.

preferences.neighbourRelation: placed where the visibility raster shows a dead zone

vibe.palette: Grey rock, silver lake, green marsh.
vibe.signatureFeature: A rock bench above the whole basin with a wind-shelter of piled stone and a scratched diagram of the three river mouths on the back wall.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance: type 'vista-ledge' runs 5 province-wide against a countBand of 4-4, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

places.name: The Long Sleep

why.founding: A daril house in a city with a large transient population of people who have recently been released from somewhere.
why.siteAdvantages: On the water's edge under a boardwalk, entered from below at low water.
why.occupantsMotive: Daril from the eastern marsh, sold by the hour, in a room where nobody asks where anyone has been.
why.pressures: The withdrawal house takes its custom from here, and the two have an arrangement neither will describe.
why.wouldChangeIf: A supply interruption from the fermentary would empty it in a week.

hardConstraints: a mooring is half the type

preferences.neighbourRelation: in a port, a market town or a slum quarter

vibe.palette: Green underlight, hammock canvas, smoke.
vibe.signatureFeature: A low room under a boardwalk with hammocks slung in three tiers and a water-level door that only opens at half tide.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance: type 'vice-den' runs 6 province-wide against a countBand of 4-5, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

places.name: Yeller's Holding

why.founding: An estate whose owning family died out in the rebellion and whose tenants, the city and a claimant from Cyrodiil have all claimed it since.
why.siteAdvantages: Good drained ground on the western feeder with a landing and a mill.
why.occupantsMotive: The tenants farm it and pay rent into an escrow the arbiter holds, which is a legal fiction everyone finds convenient.
why.pressures: The escrow is now a substantial sum and at least two parties want the case settled for that reason alone.
why.wouldChangeIf: A ruling in any direction would end a hundred-year arrangement that currently works.

hardConstraints: controls a crossing or a landing

preferences.neighbourRelation: holds the crossing its neighbours must use

vibe.signatureFeature: An estate with a sealed and shuttered great house, a fully working farm around it, and a rent chest in the arbiter's parlour eight kilometres away.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance: type 'estate-village' runs 4 province-wide against a countBand of 3-3, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

places.name: Bare Lake

why.founding: The lake's shallow southern arm empties for six weeks every dry season, exposing four square kilometres of bed that is underwater the rest of the year.
why.siteAdvantages: A wide flat arm barely a metre deep, with an outlet that drops below its sill in the dry.
why.occupantsMotive: Everyone. The drawdown is a local event: the whole shore walks out onto the bed and takes what the year has dropped.
why.pressures: Grave-stakes from a drowned burial ground stand exposed during the drawdown, which forces an annual argument about what may be taken.
why.wouldChangeIf: A wetter cycle would end the drawdown and the whole annual custom with it.

preferences.neighbourRelation: the lake region's signature seasonal event

notableNpcSlots: stall-holder who only exists six weeks a year

vibe.silhouette: For six weeks a year, a cracked grey plain with drowned fence lines and bleached stakes standing out of it; the rest of the year, open water with nothing above the surface.
vibe.palette: Cracked grey mud, bleached stake, bright sky.
vibe.materials: Cracked lake-bed clay, drowned fence timber, bleached grave-stakes, lost cargo; the only structures are the temporary market stalls that appear on the bed itself.
vibe.signatureFeature: A cracked lake bed walked by half the district, with drowned fence lines, lost cargo and standing grave-stakes emerging for six weeks a year.
vibe.condition: Exists and ceases to exist annually; nothing on it is maintained because nothing on it survives the refill.
vibe.mood: Festival with a taboo in it.

places.name: The Windlass Reckoning

why.founding: The western feeder has a two-hundred-metre rock narrows no laden hull can pass, so hulls are dragged around it.
why.siteAdvantages: A low saddle beside the narrows where a greased timber slipway can be laid on a workable gradient.
why.occupantsMotive: A drag crew with a windlass, paid by the hull, who also control who goes upstream and when.
why.pressures: The crew's monopoly is total and their maintenance of the slipway is minimal.
why.wouldChangeIf: Blasting the narrows would open the western route and end the crew.

preferences.neighbourRelation: a mandatory node on a boat lane

notableNpcSlots: windlass master who sets the queue order

vibe.silhouette: A greased timber ramp cut over a low saddle with a windlass frame at the crest, and hull-shapes queued out of sight at both ends.
vibe.palette: Grease black, pale timber, white water below.
vibe.materials: Greased hardwood skids on a laid stone bed, a hand-windlass of oak and iron, scaffold shear-legs, roller stock; the whole works is one machine and it is made of two materials.
vibe.signatureFeature: A greased timber slipway over a saddle with a hand-windlass at the top and a queue of hulls waiting at both ends.
vibe.condition: Heavily worked and constantly re-greased; the skids are replaced twice a year, the stone bed is Imperial and untouched.
vibe.approach: You hear the whitewater and the windlass together, and the queue tells you how long your day is going to be.
vibe.senses: Hulls dragging on grease, the windlass pawl, whitewater below and out of sight, tallow and hot timber, crews waiting badly.

places.name: The Stair Rapids

why.founding: The western feeder drops through a limestone stair of six ledges, which is the reason the portage exists at all.

why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. It is run empty by drag-crew apprentices as a rite and occasionally kills one.
why.pressures: It is the boundary between the basin's economy and eastern Blackwood's, and it is not negotiable.
why.wouldChangeIf: Cutting one ledge would let empty hulls run it and halve the portage trade.

preferences.neighbourRelation: forces every boat route to stop; a portage or a ferry always answers it

vibe.palette: White water, grey limestone, green over.
vibe.signatureFeature: Six clean limestone drops in a row with a worn path beside them and a name cut beside each drop.

places.name: The Counting Ground

why.founding: Where Blackrose buried the Knahaten dead of three peoples, in the order they died and without distinguishing between them.
why.siteAdvantages: A gravel terrace above the flood, the only ground in the basin that would take that many graves.
why.occupantsMotive: A memorial rota that includes Argonian grave-singers and nobody else, because nobody else is left to send anyone.
why.pressures: Two of the three peoples buried here are extinct, and the third does their remembering.
why.wouldChangeIf: Any attempt to separate the burials by people would be both impossible and obscene.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on the Umbriel corridor, in the burn country, or at a flu-emptied village

why.occupantsMotive: Nobody now. It was a village-sized pen with a fence, a gate, a ration store and a burial ground that is larger than the village.
why.pressures: This is the answer to the unclear fate of a whole people, and Blackrose has never once discussed it.
why.wouldChangeIf: Anyone who published the ration ledgers would make the city's founding families answer for it.

preferences.neighbourRelation: deliberately just out of reach of its neighbours

vibe.silhouette: A rectangular fence enclosure with a burial ground four times its size beyond it — the built thing is small and the consequence is enormous.
vibe.palette: Grey weathered fence, sour green ground, white bone.
vibe.materials: Weathered grey fence timber with the gate furniture on the outside, a ration store built into the wall, mud-mother houses inside, no stakes over any of the graves.
vibe.signatureFeature: A fenced village-sized enclosure with the gate on the outside of the fence, a ration store built into the wall, and a burial ground four times the size of the enclosure.
vibe.condition: Sixteen centuries weathered and never dismantled — the fence is falling and no one will pull it down.
vibe.approach: The fence line is visible from the road, and the fence faces inward.
vibe.senses: Nothing living inside the fence; wind through palings; sour ground; and a burial field with no carving on it anywhere, which is the loudest thing about it.

places.name: The Singing Ponds

why.founding: A farm breeding frogs selected for their call rather than their meat, because the province's chime-and-instrument trade pays better than the food trade.

why.occupantsMotive: Tone-selected stock takes six generations to fix and sells for absurd money to instrument villages.

preferences.neighbourRelation: supplies a named artisan village

places.name: The Gar Pens

places.name: Cassia's Ground

places.name: The Last Survey

why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. The instruments were carried away; the pegs and the levelling book were not.
why.pressures: The book proves the canal was feasible, which is a politically significant fact in a basin that lives on portage tolls.

preferences.neighbourRelation: chained along a planned route

places.name: Fort Cordon

why.wouldChangeIf: Permanent occupation by any faction would give them the southern road.

preferences.neighbourRelation: on a dead road

why.founding: A Kothringi village of the people canon places in the Blackrose region, emptied by the Knahaten Flu in a single season.

why.pressures: The Flu is the founding trauma of half the province's demography, and this is what it actually looks like on the ground.
why.wouldChangeIf: Proof that the ground is safe would put a village back on it within a year.

hardConstraints: coastal and riverine — they were sea-going

preferences.neighbourRelation: in the west and centre, where the Kothringi lived

vibe.palette: Pale plaster, black doorway, bright river.
vibe.materials: Pale lime plaster over rubble on a Kothringi plan; storage pits still lidded; no Argonian or Imperial rebuild anywhere on the site.
vibe.signatureFeature: Silver-skinned people's houses of a form found nowhere else in the province, standing to head height, with the flu-year's stores still in the pits.

places.name: Spine

why.founding: A village built as one continuous boardwalk out from the shore into the lake, extended a house at a time for three centuries.
why.siteAdvantages: A shallow shelf that runs eight hundred metres out from the shore before it drops.
why.occupantsMotive: Position on the spine is seniority: the oldest households are at the shore end and the newest are over deep water.
why.pressures: The far end is now over the drop and each new house is more expensive and less safe than the last.
why.wouldChangeIf: A storm surge would take the outer third and reset the village's whole social order.

hardConstraints: crosses water rather than sitting beside it

preferences.neighbourRelation: often the only dry route through its stretch

places.name: The Barge Yard

why.occupantsMotive: Crews dive for cargo, not hulls; the toll families buy the recovered goods at a discount that reflects who they are.

why.wouldChangeIf: A rise in the lake would put the wrecks out of free-diving range entirely.

preferences.neighbourRelation: always paired with drowned ground it works

places.name: Under-Longmont

why.siteAdvantages: It stands in five to eight metres of clear cold lake water, complete, because nobody demolished anything — they simply left.
why.occupantsMotive: Nobody. Longmont's households still know which house down there was theirs.

why.wouldChangeIf: A drop in lake level would expose it and force a decision about who owns what.

preferences.neighbourRelation: below a living settlement, or beside one that watched it go

vibe.signatureFeature: A complete village standing upright underwater with its roofs intact, its street legible, and grave-stakes still standing in rows on its drowned burial ground.

places.deferredWhy: Parked in the imperial-penal-south over-density rebalance: type 'drowned-village' runs 4 province-wide against a countBand of 3-3, so the surplus is paid out of the over-band types first.

places.name: The North Stage

why.occupantsMotive: A city concession, run efficiently, which is unusual enough here to be remarked on.

why.wouldChangeIf: A crossing further north would bypass the city's count entirely.

hardConstraints: across water too deep or wide to ford

preferences.neighbourRelation: a mandatory node in the route graph; has a paired stage

places.name: The Cluster

why.occupantsMotive: Nobody owns lake bottom; the cluster's entire legal position is that it does not touch anything.

preferences.neighbourRelation: has two or three fixed moorings keyed to the flood cycle

vibe.signatureFeature: A back-channel house whose front room is a working counting office with proper books, and whose back room is not.

places.name: Robbed City

places.name: The Meer Camp

places.name: Longmont

why.pressures: A city that remembers raising an army looks at these lines every day.

hardConstraints: dry ground with a view of the target

preferences.neighbourRelation: always paired with what it besieged

places.name: The Arbiter's House

why.pressures: The correct attribution is legible in the building itself to anyone who compares it with the Robbed City.
why.wouldChangeIf: A correct identification would embarrass an institution and change who has a claim on the site.

preferences.neighbourRelation: near a settlement that tells the story wrong

vibe.signatureFeature: A ruin with two competing carved attribution plaques at its entrance, both wrong, and the answer visible in the masonry twenty paces inside.
